name: Adams County

actions.title: (City of Brighton) Meta data center campus approval
actions.summary: The City of Brighton approved Meta's plans for a large data center campus in the area, part of Meta's broader national expansion. The project brought discussions around water use and power infrastructure.

contextBlurb: Adams County, including the City of Brighton, has become a target for hyperscale data center development due to available land and proximity to Denver metro infrastructure. Water consumption in semi-arid Colorado is a key concern for local officials and residents.

name: Weld County

actions.title: Large-scale data center development near Platteville
actions.summary: Weld County approved site plans for data center facilities taking advantage of available land and energy infrastructure in the northern Colorado corridor. Discussions included grid capacity and economic development benefits.

contextBlurb: Weld County's open land and energy infrastructure (including proximity to natural gas resources) have made it attractive for data center developers. County officials have weighed economic benefits against infrastructure impacts.

name: Boulder County

actions.title: Six-Month Moratorium on Data Center Applications
actions.summary: Boulder County commissioners unanimously imposed a six-month moratorium on accepting data center applications in unincorporated areas while staff drafts Land Use Code definitions and siting rules.

contextBlurb: Boulder County paused data center applications in unincorporated areas for six months beginning June 2, 2026. Commissioners cited the absence of a specific data center use in the Land Use Code and directed staff to determine appropriate definitions, scales, locations, and potential prohibitions.

name: Woodland Park

actions.title: 18-Month Data Center Application Moratorium (Ordinance 1525)
actions.summary: Woodland Park adopted an 18-month moratorium on submitting, accepting, processing, or approving data center applications while the city develops zoning, land-use, water, and infrastructure standards.

contextBlurb: Woodland Park enacted an 18-month pause in July 2026 because its code lacked standards tailored to data centers' unusually large electricity and water requirements. The city will use the period to draft local rules and monitor possible statewide legislation in Colorado's 2027 session.
